name: attribute-dictionary

slugs.covers: practical abilities: driving, swimming, cooking level
technical skills, stacks mastered, and specific systems or codebases they know deeply
a standing organisation in this person's arrangements that is not the employer or institutional affiliation (bank, gym, insurer, clinic, vendor) - what it IS, never its current state
a standing named third party in this person's life not covered by relationship.* (dentist, landlord, accountant, client, mentor) - who they ARE, never what they did

a standing place in this person's life beyond identity.* (office building, the branch or clinic they use, a second home, a child's school) - a fixed point in their routine, never where something happened
years of experience, seniority stage, and career transitions (not the current title)

en: how long they have done this

slugs.covers: education: current or planned enrolment (institution, level or year, major or field, courses being taken) AND completed history and degrees
employment arrangement: employed, freelance, contractor, founder, between roles, retired, studying full time
industry or sector worked in (not the job title, not the named employer)
standing affiliation with an institution that is not the employer: lab, university, open-source org, professional body
the person's standing role on or ownership of a project, service or system

ja: プロジェクトでの役割

slugs.covers: the team or group the person belongs to (the person's membership, not the team as an entity)
the timezone the person operates in

en: what time zone they are in

ja: テクノロジーへの関心
ポッドキャストの好み
プラットフォームの好み
プログラミング言語の好み

slugs.covers: travel taste — destinations, styles and modes of travel the user likes or dislikes; a wished-for trip is goal.travel
how they work WITH OTHERS: meetings, code and design review, delegation, conflict, mentoring. Not one-to-one message style
how to talk to THEM: answer length, tone, formality, channel, and how they want feedback delivered. Not the subject matter, not how work is organised

en: how they want things written down
ja: コミュニケーションスタイル
ドキュメントの書き方

slugs.covers: a hard limit the person states that bounds what can be recommended: hardware ceiling, compliance rule, pinned version, available effort. NOT a preference — a preference can be argued with, a constraint cannot
standing craft practices and stances on how work is done: testing discipline, review habits, what they read first

revision_note: 2026-08-18 revision, owner ruling: removed 8 slugs that hold a value which changes or that describe something other than the person - finance.income, finance.net_worth, health.body (body metrics is a reading), identity (bare catch-all), entity.event, entity.pet (duplicate of relationship.pets), entity.product, entity.project (the slot a moving project budget entered through). Added preference.weather. Narrowed entity.person / entity.organization / entity.place to identity only, never current state. 2026-08-16 revision: +9 slugs (industry, career_history, employment_status, team_membership, project_role, institutional_affiliation, timezone, trait.practice, trait.constraint), widened identity.education and ability.technical, removed trait.documentation / preference.general / entity.team, tightened trait.communication and trait.collaboration. Merged names carried as synonyms so the normalizing matcher resolves them: documentation -> trait.communication, team -> entity.organization. preference.general is DELIBERATELY unmapped — an unmappable preference must store WITHOUT a key, which is the correct behaviour and the reason the slot was removed. Merge synonyms are the OLD FULL SLUG NAMES (entity.team, trait.documentation), not bare words: a bare 'team' is legitimately owned by identity.team_membership, and an ambiguous key must resolve to nothing rather than to whichever entry was indexed first.
